clue.text: It can put a gloss on an obscure passage

definitions.text: It can put a gloss on an obscure passage

parts.words: It can put a gloss on an obscure passage
parts.note: reads like a scholar's commentary explaining a difficult text, but describes a coating brushed over a dark corridor to give it a shine

explanation.surface: Something that annotates a hard-to-understand piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gloss' suggests a footnote and 'obscure passage' a puzzling bit of text; in fact the gloss is a shiny finish and the passage a dim hallway.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloss is a shiny finish applied with a brush, so a decorator's coating can literally gloss a gloomy hallway.

clue.text: In a hurry, so take a wild shot in stick-up

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to paste is to stick something up, as on a wall

indicators.note: a wild version of the word shot has its letters scrambled

explanation.surface: Hastily taking a random shot during a hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick-up' suggests a robbery; it is PASTE. 'wild' makes OSTH from SHOT, and 'in' places that inside PASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: With great speed, as fast as the old mail riders could travel.

clue.text: Language of love in the S of France coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top
one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: the Midi is the south of France
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Romantic talk in Provence rising to the fore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside MIDI to give MOIDI; 'coming up' turns that around in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a characteristic form of expression, so a manner of speech or dialect.

clue.text: Routine drudgery of the wine factory?

definitions.meaning: dull, repetitive work that goes nowhere
humorously, a mill where grapes are trodden underfoot

explanation.walkthrough: Grapes were traditionally trodden to make wine, so a 'tread mill' would be a winery.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotonous work is likened to the endless walking wheel, and a place where grapes are trodden would jokingly be called a mill.

clue.text: Complaint that may have to be dealt with in the Appendix

definitions.text: Complaint that may have to be dealt with in the Appendix

parts.words: Complaint that may have to be dealt with in the Appendix
parts.note: reads like a reader's grievance sent to the back pages of a book, but means a medical complaint of the appendix organ, the kind surgeons remove

explanation.surface: A grievance that must be handled in the appendix at the back of a report.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'grumbling appendix' is a phrase for a mildly, repeatedly inflamed appendix; the answer is both a complaint in the sense of whingeing and the illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Whingeing is a form of complaint, and a recurrent mild inflammation of the appendix is idiomatically called a grumbling one.

clue.text: Leave with pain after kind of turn, but may, be a good colour

indicators.note: the pain piece follows the turn piece

parts.note: to go is to leave
a U-turn, giving U
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Instructions to depart in pain after some kind of manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind of turn' is a U-turn, giving just the letter U.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouache is opaque watercolour paint, so a good medium for colour.

clue.text: Expel from burrow that's damaging the Arun

indicators.note: damaging the words breaks them up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something harming the River Arun drives creatures out of their holes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Arun is a river in Sussex, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig an animal out of its earth or den, as with a fox.

clue.text: Blunder by Law, we hear

indicators.note: the word is judged by its sound, as if heard spoken

parts.note: Andrew Bonar Law was a British prime minister in 1922-23

explanation.surface: A gaffe made by a statesman, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Law' looks like legislation; it is Bonar Law, the Conservative prime minister, whose first name sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An American informal word for a silly mistake or howler.

clue.text: The press etc in time changing without delay

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other
the word time is changed, its letters scrambled

parts.note: the media are the press, broadcasting and so on

explanation.surface: Newspapers and the like changing over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' makes IMTE from TIME, and 'in' places MEDIA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Instant, happening at once with no interval.

clue.text: Darling who didn't live in a Wendy house

definitions.text: Darling who didn't live in a Wendy house

parts.words: Darling who didn't live in a Wendy house
parts.note: Darling suggests Wendy Darling of Peter Pan, whose playhouse gave the Wendy house its name; the other famous Darling, the Victorian rescuer, lived in a lighthouse

explanation.surface: A sweetheart who never lived in a child's playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace Darling, a Northumberland lighthouse keeper's daughter, became a heroine in 1838 rowing out to rescue shipwreck survivors; Wendy Darling is the girl in Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian heroine lived in the Longstone lighthouse, not the playhouse built for Wendy in Peter Pan.

clue.text: Quick results from this device for moving logs

definitions.text: Quick results from this device for moving logs

parts.words: Quick results from this device for moving logs
parts.note: logs suggests timber being shifted, but they are logarithms, which this calculating instrument adds by sliding one scale along another

explanation.surface: A machine that gets timber shifted fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'logs' looks like lumber; it is short for logarithms, which the pre-calculator instrument moved along its scales to multiply quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The old engineer's calculating stick multiplied numbers by sliding logarithmic scales against each other, giving fast answers.

clue.text: Place where the lion had a nerve

definitions.text: Place where the lion had a nerve

parts.words: Place where the lion had a nerve
parts.note: points to the valley in Greek myth where a fearsome lion lived until Hercules strangled it as his first labour; the lion's nerve is its boldness in terrorising the area

explanation.surface: The spot where a big cat showed some courage.
explanation.walkthrough: Hercules' first labour was killing the lion of this valley in the Peloponnese, a beast whose hide no weapon could pierce.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek valley gave its name to the invulnerable lion of myth slain by Hercules.

clue.text: Like -hothouse atmosphere in which Polly Peachum idled

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the words that follow, tucked in the run spanning the surname and the verb

explanation.surface: Polly Peachum, heroine of The Beggar's Opera, lazes about in a steamy greenhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' signals the run of letters across 'PeacHUM IDled'. Polly Peachum is a character in John Gay's The Beggar's Opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothouse is kept warm and moist, so its air is damp and muggy.

clue.text: Kind of paper used for reports?

definitions.text: Kind of paper used for reports?

parts.words: Kind of paper used for reports?
parts.note: reports suggests written documents, but here means bangs from a gun; the answer is both a thick drawing paper and the case holding a gun's charge

explanation.surface: A sort of stationery you would write reports on.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'report' is also the sound of a gunshot, and the answer names both the heavy paper and the ammunition round.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick drawing paper is called by this name, and so is the shell of a gun's charge that produces a bang.

clue.text: Realist made cross at St Andrew's

indicators.note: the letters of the word realist are made into something else, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A realist got angry while at St Andrews in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made cross' reads as 'angered', but 'made' alone is the anagram signal and 'cross' starts the definition. St Andrew's cross is the diagonal X of the Scottish flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The heraldic term for a diagonal X-shaped cross, as on Scotland's flag of St Andrew.

clue.text: Can this unmercenary union inflame passion?

definitions.text: Can this unmercenary union inflame passion?

parts.words: Can this unmercenary union inflame passion?
parts.note: a marriage not made for money; read cryptically, a match is something that can set alight, and the thing it would ignite is love

explanation.surface: Asking whether a marriage not made for money can stir up desire.
explanation.walkthrough: A match lights fires, so a match that inflames passion (love) is a pun on the phrase for a marriage of affection.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage made for affection rather than wealth or status.

clue.text: Plant that could be the ruin of Women's Lib?

definitions.text: Plant that could be the ruin of Women's Lib?

parts.words: Plant that could be the ruin of Women's Lib?
parts.note: reads as a mole or spy wrecking the feminist movement, but splits into a female bird and a curse: the bane of hens, a poisonous weed

explanation.surface: An infiltrator who might destroy the feminist movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a planted spy; it is a poisonous herb whose name splits as HEN (slang for a woman) and BANE (ruin).
explanation.definitionFit: The poisonous nightshade-family herb is named as if it were the curse of poultry.

clue.text: Fix huntsman's trophy in the bath-room

definitions.note: the definition describes where the item is kept, standing for a thing found in the bathroom

parts.note: to nail is to fix in place
the brush is a fox's tail, kept by fox hunters as a trophy

explanation.surface: Mounting a fox-hunter's trophy on the bathroom wall.
explanation.walkthrough: In British fox hunting the fox's bushy tail, its brush, was awarded as a trophy. The definition is loose: an item found in the bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stiff scrubber for cleaning fingernails, kept by the washbasin.

clue.text: It's the making of the Law!

definitions.text: It's the making of the Law!

parts.words: It's the making of the Law!
parts.note: sounds like praise, as when something is the making of a person, but literally describes the passing of legislation

explanation.surface: Something that turns out to be the making of the legal profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the making of' usually means the thing that improves someone; here it is literal, the creation of a statute.
explanation.definitionFit: The process of passing a bill into a statute.

clue.text: Hide letter dropped from mail carrier

indicators.note: one piece is taken away from the thing that carries mail, leaving the rest

parts.note: an envelope is what a letter is posted in
E is a letter of the alphabet, the one removed here

explanation.surface: Concealing a letter that fell out of the postman's bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' suggests something posted; it means a single letter of the alphabet, E, taken from the end of ENVELOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap something completely is to conceal it from view.

clue.text: Make a meaningful sound when you call me

parts.note: to phone is to call

explanation.surface: An instruction to say something worthwhile when you ring.
explanation.walkthrough: A phoneme is the smallest unit of sound that distinguishes meaning in a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguists' term for the smallest unit of speech that distinguishes one word from another.

clue.text: Wild idea may ring a bell with an artist

parts.note: to chime is to make a bell ring
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A crazy notion might strike a chord with a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring a bell' seems to mean 'seem familiar'; here it is literal, to chime.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanciful, impossible notion is named after the fire-breathing monster of Greek myth.

clue.text: Find fault — nothing right with cover for driver

parts.note: to carp is to complain pettily
zero, written O

explanation.surface: Complaining about there being no right turn for a motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' could be a golf club; it is a motorist, whose vehicle sits under this shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-sided roofed shelter beside a house for parking a vehicle.

clue.text: Vain display with a severe hair-style

parts.note: pomp is showy, empty ceremony
dour means stern and grim

explanation.surface: Showing off while sporting a harsh haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: The swept-up hairdo is named after Madame de Pompadour, mistress of Louis XV.
explanation.definitionFit: A swept-up, high-volume coiffure named after Louis XV's mistress.

clue.text: Deposit on a jacket

parts.note: to park is to put down or deposit

explanation.surface: Paying a deposit on a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposit' looks like a down payment; it is a verb, to park.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded windproof coat, originally an Inuit garment.

clue.text: Summer creeper

definitions.meaning: one who sums, a person adding up figures
a snake, which creeps along the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' is not the season but someone who does sums; 'creeper' is not a plant but a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A calculator does addition, and the common European viper slithers along the ground.

clue.text: Intransigent supporter of a Large part of the Bible

parts.note: big means large
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A stubborn fan of a big section of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: An intolerant, unbending partisan who will not accept other views.

clue.text: Port in this cake?

definitions.meaning: a harbour city in north-west Italy
a rich fruit cake topped with almonds named after that Italian city

explanation.walkthrough: Genoa cake is a British fruit cake with almonds on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ligurian harbour city gives its name to a rich almond-topped fruit cake.

clue.text: Estimated value of orchid in two words

definitions.text: value of orchid in two words
definitions.meaning: split the flower name as OR CHID; chid, the old past tense of chide, means scolded, and this word is also an old verb for scolding

explanation.walkthrough: Split the flower's name into OR CHID: the second word, chid (scolded), has the same meaning as the answer in its old sense of telling off.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess a worth is to give it a value; the archaic verb for berating someone also takes this form, matching chid.

clue.text: Athens, Milton's "mother of arts and -"

parts.note: a quotation to complete: in Paradise Regained Milton calls Athens the eye of Greece and the mother of arts and of fine speaking

explanation.surface: A line from Milton praising the city of Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton, Paradise Regained IV: 'Athens, the eye of Greece, mother of arts and' the missing word, the gift of fluent persuasive speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluent, persuasive oratory, the gift for which Athens was famed.

clue.text: Born hater can easily become hateful

indicators.note: the letters of the two words can be turned into another arrangement, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone born to hate may readily turn odious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something detestable is loathsome and inspires disgust.

clue.text: Midlothian's seat of love

definitions.meaning: Scott's novel The ... of Midlothian, also the name of an Edinburgh football club, takes its title from the old Tolbooth prison
the organ traditionally held to be where affection resides

explanation.walkthrough: The Heart of Midlothian is a Walter Scott novel and an Edinburgh football club; Midlothian is the Scottish county round Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: The chest organ is conventionally the home of affection, and it completes Scott's title about Midlothian.
